rationale: The base station auto-updated to firmware 4.5, which drops support for the legacy v2 radio protocol. The Living Motion sensor (SEN-M1) was still on firmware 1.1 speaking v2, producing E-305 "protocol v2 not supported" and a connected_no_events state. An OTA upgrade to v1.4 (v3 protocol) resolved the issue and alerts resumed.

repair_steps: Confirm the Living Motion sensor (SEN-M1) is now on firmware v1.4 and status is online with events flowing.
Verify no other devices are on legacy v2 protocol; if any, trigger OTA upgrade to v3-compatible firmware.
Clear the E-305 error from the base station log and confirm no new errors appear.
Advise customer that the issue is resolved and alerts will function normally.
output.customer_reply: We've updated your Living Motion sensor to the latest firmware, which is compatible with your base station's recent update. The sensor is now reconnected and sending alerts as expected. No further action is needed from your side. If you notice any other devices not responding, please let us know. Thank you for your patience!

results.text: The peripheral firmware speaks a radio protocol the base station no longer supports, or vice versa. Frontline action: trigger OTA upgrade of the peripheral. If OTA is not available for the device or fails twice, escalate to FAE as protocol conflict.

Base station firmware updates are pushed automatically at night. HB-200 firmware 4.5 removes support for the legacy v2 radio protocol. Peripherals still running v2 firmware must be upgraded to v3 firmware before or after the base station update, otherwise they disconnect.
